title: Equivariant internal binomial-basis contraction of polynomial differences
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed $\mathbf Q$-algebra on the coherent profinite site, meaning a commutative condensed ring with a unit-preserving map from the constant rational ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use ordinary internal $A$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Fix $d\geq0$ and let $B=A[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$ be the internal direct sum of copies of $A$ on its monomials, with coefficientwise addition and monomial multiplication [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $G$ be a profinite group (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), and give $B$ an internal $A$-linear $G$-action by algebra automorphisms, natural on all profinite test sets [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Put $T=B[y]=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}B\,y^n$ internally and extend $G$ coefficientwise, fixing $y$. Define the $B$-linear internal endomorphism $\Delta$ by $\Delta f(y)=f(y-1)-f(y)$.

Put $b_0=1$ and
$$b_n=\frac{(-1)^n}{n!}y(y+1)\cdots(y+n-1)\qquad(n>0).$$
The maps from the internal copies of $B$ given by the $b_n$ exhibit $T$ as their direct sum: expansion in these $b_n$ is unique and finite on each monomial. In particular the change from $y^n$ to $b_n$ is triangular with invertible rational diagonal entries. The internal formulas satisfy $\Delta b_0=0$ and $\Delta b_n=b_{n-1}$ for $n>0$.

Let $i:B\to T$ include constants, let $p:T\to B$ be evaluation at $y=0$, and let $J:T\to T$ be the $B$-linear map $J(b_n)=b_{n+1}$. All these maps are internal and $G$-equivariant, finite on each monomial, and compatible with every profinite base change. They satisfy
$$\Delta J=1_T,\qquad J\Delta=1_T-ip,\qquad pi=1_B,\qquad\Delta i=0.$$
Consequently the chain maps $i:B[0]\to[T\xrightarrow{\Delta}T]$ and $p:[T\xrightarrow{\Delta}T]\to B[0]$ are a chain homotopy equivalence, with homotopy $J$ from degree one to degree zero. In the ordinary derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] their classes give inverse isomorphisms
$$B[0]\cong Q[\,T\xrightarrow{\Delta}T\,]\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal A_G(A)),$$
where the displayed complex is in degrees $0,1$. The assertions include $d=0$, $G=1$ and the zero algebra; they require neither a topology on polynomial degrees nor completion of the direct sums.

proof.text: Work with the internal direct sum specified in the statement. A finite rational matrix between finite sums of copies of $B$ defines an internal $B$-linear map, by addition and rational scalar multiplication in the module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. More generally, a matrix with finitely many nonzero entries in each column defines a map out of the direct sum: specify its map on each summand and use the coproduct universal property. Equalities of such maps are checked on the summand inclusions. Thus finite polynomial calculations below define internal morphisms; they do not assume that evaluating a sheaf coproduct commutes with taking sections.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: interpretation of finite-on-each-monomial formulas

proof.text: Write $b_n=u_ny^n+\sum_{k<n}c_{nk}y^k$, where $u_n=(-1)^n/n!\in\mathbf Q^\times$ and $c_{nk}\in\mathbf Q$. Expansion of the finite product defining $b_n$ gives this equality, also for $n=0$ with $u_0=1$. Recursively define $e_0=b_0$ and $e_n=u_n^{-1}(b_n-\sum_{k<n}c_{nk}e_k)$; here the recursion expresses each monomial $y^n$ as a finite combination of the formal $b$-summands. Induction on $n$ shows that substitution into monomials sends $e_n$ to $y^n$, and substitution of these expansions into $b_n$ gives back its formal summand. Both composites are therefore identity on every summand. This constructs inverse internal triangular maps by step 1, proves the direct-sum assertion and uniqueness, and does not cancel a nonzero element of $B$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: finite triangular inverse, by induction on the monomial index

proof.text: Put $P_0(y)=1$ and $P_n(y)=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(y+j)$ for $n>0$. For $n\geq1$ the common-factor calculation is $P_n(y-1)-P_n(y)=((y-1)-(y+n-1))P_{n-1}(y)=-nP_{n-1}(y)$. The empty product makes this valid for $n=1$. Multiplication by $(-1)^n/n!$ gives $\Delta b_n=b_{n-1}$; direct substitution gives $\Delta b_0=0$. These are identities of formal polynomials over $\mathbf Q$, hence identities of the internal maps from each $B$-summand. No assertion about injectivity of evaluating polynomials as functions is used.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: rising-factorial difference identity

proof.text: In the coordinates of step 2, define $J$ by shifting the $n$th summand to the $(n+1)$st. This is an internal map by the coproduct property; conjugating by the triangular maps makes it the specified $B$-linear endomorphism of $T$. Each of $i,p,J,\Delta$ has a finite rational formula on each $y$-monomial, with $p(b_0)=1$ and $p(b_n)=0$ for $n>0$. For every profinite parameter set $S$ and $g\in C(S,G)$, coefficientwise action fixes these rational scalars and $y$, so both orders of applying any map and $g$ send $c b_n$ to the same indicated rational combination with coefficient $g(c)$. The maps are therefore equivariant in the sense of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. Restrictions preserve rational scalars, sums and products, so these same equations hold after every profinite base change.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: construction and natural equivariance of the summand shift

proof.text: Check on the $b_n$-summands. Step 3 gives $\Delta J(b_n)=b_n$ for all $n$; it gives $J\Delta(b_0)=0$ and $J\Delta(b_n)=b_n$ for $n>0$. By the values of $p$ in step 4 these are precisely $\Delta J=1_T$ and $J\Delta=1_T-ip$. Also $pi=1_B$ and $\Delta i=0$ hold on constants. The coproduct property extends the equations to the internal maps, including when the coefficient algebra is zero.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: the four deformation-retraction identities

proof.text: Let $C$ be $T\xrightarrow{\Delta}T$ in degrees $0,1$. Define the cochain map $i:B[0]\to C$ in degree zero by inclusion and the cochain map $p:C\to B[0]$ in degree zero by evaluation, with zero components elsewhere. Their chain conditions are respectively $\Delta i=0$ and a zero equality. Define $h^1=J:C^1\to C^0$ and all other $h^q=0$. The equation $1_C-ip=dh+hd$ in degree zero is $1_T-ip=J\Delta$, and in degree one is $1_T=\Delta J$; elsewhere both sides vanish. Together with $pi=1$ this is the asserted cochain homotopy equivalence. All components are equivariant by step 4.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-written algebraic input: explicit cochain maps and degree-minus-one homotopy

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-condensed-product-action-inflation] with $R=A$ and the second group trivial: its abelian-category assertion supplies $\mathcal A_G(A)$. The identity $J\Delta=1-ip$ identifies $i:B\to T$ with the categorical kernel of $\Delta$: any $a:M\to T$ killed by $\Delta$ satisfies $a=ip a$, uniquely since $pi=1$. The identity $\Delta J=1$ makes $\Delta$ a split epimorphism, so its cokernel is zero. Hence $H^0(C)\cong B$, $H^1(C)=0$, and all other cohomology is zero, with $H^0(i)$ the specified identification. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $i$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $Q(i)$ is invertible. Functoriality gives $Q(p)Q(i)=1$, so $Q(p)=Q(i)^{-1}$ and also $Q(i)Q(p)=1$. This proves the displayed derived isomorphism with the stated maps. The proof never used the number of spectator variables or a nontrivial group or algebra, so includes $d=0$, $G=1$ and the zero algebra.
